title: RWB-S8-E7001-APP: the X1 slice has no plan row for its two cross-service reads, no event names, no complaint service level and no published case-clock boundary, and its happy path has no acceptance criterion
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R7.2, R7.3 and R9; context pack S8 rwb-deviation; split plan story line RWB-S8-E7001-APP; FSD S8 Deviation handling v3 A2.1 to A2.6, A2.10, A1.2, A1.4 and Screens; TSD S8 Deviation handling v2 T2, T3.1, T3.2, T4, T5.2, T5.3, T6.1 and T-A.1; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 DEV route set; legacy RWB-E7-001
section: Metadata (Depends on (build), Contract dependencies, Integration dependencies, External dependencies); Sections 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 11, 12.1 to 12.4, 14 and 18
description: (1) The story line gives H = RWB-S8-E7001-CON, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON with C, I and X empty, while the feature names the Document hub as an integration point and the S8 row of the connection matrix gives the service a REST and an event call to rwb-source-data, so the evidence pack and the customer facts are consumed with no plan row. (2) The Ownership Map gives S8 two events as EV-06 and EV-07 with no names and no topic, while TSD S8 T5.3 names DeviationRaised and DeviationCleared and the naming rule gives rwb.deviation.events.v1. (3) The X1 complaint service level is the metric target 'Set with DL22' and no source publishes a value, while R-DEV-20 escalates at 10 working days. (4) No source publishes how the stage clock is paused on behalf of a stage: rwb-case owns timer, queue and assignment and the boundary is Temporal. (5) The split plan gives this slice AC2 only, so the happy path of X1 (legacy AC1) has no acceptance criterion in the APP story and TC-E7-001-01 is carried without its AC. (6) The pattern set omits DP-09 and DP-14 although the story publishes two events on the service topic. (7) SCR-08 shows a deviation queue and the Ownership Map gives S8 no read operation.
evidence: Story line RWB-S8-E7001-APP with three H rows and empty C, I and X; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-09 and DP-14 rows; connection matrix S8 row (E to P3, R E to P1, T E to P10) and column S8 (P3, P6, P9 listen); context pack S8 Events EV-06 and EV-07; FSD S8 A2.10.1 metric 'Set with DL22' and A2.10.2 'Integration points Workbench, Document hub'; TSD S8 T-A.1 and T-A.2; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DEV-01 and R-DEV-20
proposed: Keep the plan's H, C, I and X rows as they stand; record the rwb-document and rwb-source-data reads as C in fact with placeholders and fakes; adopt DeviationRaised and DeviationCleared as EV-06 and EV-07 on rwb.deviation.events.v1 with RWB-PLT-TE006-CON as the outbox library the two publications need; treat the X1 complaint service level as the DL22 value and build only the 10-working-day escalation of R-DEV-20; declare the stage clock pause as a signal in the stage outcome; prove the X1 journey where AC1 is owned and carry TC-E7-001-01 as the application half

title: RWB-S8-E7001-CON: the event names, the three consumed operation names, the status-to-message mapping, a read for SCR-08 and the test level of the legacy cases have no published baseline
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R7.2 and R9; context pack S8 rwb-deviation; split plan story line RWB-S8-E7001-CON; TSD S8 Deviation handling v2 T3.1, T3.2, T4, T5.3, T6.1 and T-A.1; FSD S8 Deviation handling v3 A2.10 and Screens; legacy RWB-E7-001
section: Metadata (Depends on (build), Contract dependencies); Sections 3, 7, 11, 12.1 to 12.5, 12.8, 14 and 16
description: (1) The Ownership Map gives the two events as EV-06 and EV-07 and TSD S8 T5.3 gives two event names, but no source pairs an id with a name. (2) The rwb-document evidence-pack read and the rwb-source-data customer-fact read have no published operation names, and the FSD names the Document hub while the S8 row of the connection matrix names no P5 call. (3) The rwb-case events the service listens to have no published names. (4) TSD S8 T-A.2 gives error sets as status codes only, with no message id per condition, so each status is bound to a legacy or FSD message. (5) SCR-08 Deviation queue shows a list of open deviations and the Ownership Map gives S8 two write operations and no read, so the baseline declares no queue read and records the gap. (6) The legacy test cases of RWB-E7-001 carry no level, so each is mapped to Contract in the CON story and to Component in the APP story. (7) The pattern set omits DP-09 and DP-14 although the baseline declares two events on the service topic.
evidence: Context pack S8 ownership rows (Tables 1, REST 2, Events EV-06 and EV-07, Jobs 0, Workflows 1); TSD S8 T-A.1 API-S8-001 and API-S8-002; T-A.2 error lists 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 503 without message ids; TSD S8 T5.3 two published events; connection matrix S8 row and column; FSD S8 A2.10.2 and the Screens table; legacy RWB-E7-001 messages MSG-S8-001, MSG-GEN-001, MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P7-003
proposed: Publish the baseline with the four placeholders and the two event names taken from TSD S8 T5.3 in the order of the Ownership Map rows; bind every error status to one message id of section 14; declare no queue read and name SCR-08 as served on the composite route by the case list; confirm the placeholders with their owners before the tag and record the tag date in the contract README
